title: rhus radicans var. laetevirens
intro: Rhus radicans var. laetevirens, commonly known as Eastern Poison Ivy, is a plant species that belongs to the Anacardiaceae family. It has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antiseptic, and antioxidant properties. The plant's therapeutic actions include treating skin conditions such as eczema, dermatitis, and wounds, as well as reducing fever and alleviating pain. The bioactive constituents of Eastern Poison Ivy include alkaloids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, which have been shown to exhibit antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant activities.
